message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to keep your piano sounding and looking its best:

| # | Tip | Why it matters |
|---|-----|----------------|
| **1** | Keep the room at stable temperature & humidity (45‑55 % RH). | Fluctuations cause wood expansion/contraction → cracks or warped soundboard. |
| **2** | Use a hygrometer + humidifier/dehumidifier as needed. | Prevents “dry” or “wet” conditions from damaging strings/keys. |
| **3** | Clean keys gently with a soft microfiber cloth after each use. | Removes oils and dust that can dull key action over time. |
| **4** | Wipe down the exterior with a mild cleaner designed for pianos. Avoid harsh chemicals. | Protects finish without stripping protective coatings. |
| **5** | Vacuum under the pedals and around the keyboard area. | Keeps debris out of moving parts and prevents dust buildup inside the case. |
| **6** | Check the pedal mechanism monthly – ensure smooth travel and no sticking. | A stuck pedal can damage internal components if left unchecked. |
| **7** | Inspect the hammers and felt regularly (every few months). Replace worn hammer heads promptly. | Maintains consistent tone quality and reduces wear on strings. |
| **8** | Tune the piano at least twice a year (or more often if you play frequently). | Tuning keeps notes accurate and helps detect early structural issues. |
| **9** | Have a professional technician perform an annual inspection (“full service”). | Detects hidden problems such as loose pins, cracked plates, or faulty escapement before they become serious. |
| **10** | Position the piano away from direct sunlight, radiators, vents, or high traffic areas. | Sunlight fades lacquer; heat causes warping; foot traffic adds vibration stress. |

### Quick Maintenance Checklist (Every Month)

- [ ] Measure humidity level.
- [ ] Lightly clean keys and surface.
- [ ] Test pedal operation.
- [ ] Listen for unusual sounds during practice.

### When to Call a Technician

- Sudden change in pitch or intonation.
- Noticeable buzzing or rattling noises.
- Keys feel sticky or unresponsive.
- Visible cracks or splintered wood.
- Any major changes in environmental conditions.

By following this routine, you'll preserve both the aesthetic beauty and acoustic integrity of your piano for years to come!
